title: Coral Lipid Assay for 96-well plates
author: Colleen B Bove
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bvcfn2tn

steps.title: Thaw coral samples
steps.instruction: Retrieve coral tissue slurry tubes from the –80 °C freezer and allow them to thaw; process a maximum of 24 samples per 96‑well plate, each in triplicate.

steps.title: Vortex and aliquot sample
steps.instruction: Vortex each thawed sample tube and transfer exactly 600 µL of the slurry into a labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare chloroform‑methanol stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh 2:1 (v/v) chloroform (CHCl₃) to methanol (CH₃OH) stock solution each day that plates will be run.

steps.title: Add solvents to sample tube
steps.instruction: To each 1.5 mL sample tube add 400 µL CHCl₃ followed by 200 µL CH₃OH, maintaining the 2:1 ratio.

steps.title: Prepare standard dilution series
steps.instruction: Create a seven‑tube standard series and perform the following actions:

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL CHCl₃ to tubes 2 through 7 (tube 1 receives no CHCl₃ at this point).
Vortex each tube briefly, then place the set on a plate shaker for 20 minutes.
Add 160 µL of 0.05 M NaCl to each tube, preserving the overall CHCl₃ : CH₃OH : NaCl volume ratio of 2 : 1 : 0.8.
Invert each tube gently two times, then open and re‑close the lid.
Centrifuge the tubes at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Carefully remove and discard the top CHCl₃ layer; then withdraw 100 µL from each tube for the assay (repeat this removal three times to obtain three 100 µL replicates).
Add 600 µL of a 1.5 mg/mL corn‑oil stock solution to tube 1.
Transfer 300 µL from tube 1 into tube 2 and back‑pipette to mix; repeat the 300 µL transfer sequentially from tube 2 to 3, 3 to 4, 4 to 5, and 5 to 6, mixing after each transfer.
Discard 300 µL from tube 6 so that its final volume is 300 µL.
Leave tube 7 as a blank containing only CHCl₃; do not add any corn‑oil standard.

steps.title: Load samples into 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of each prepared sample or standard to the appropriate wells of a 96‑well plate in triplicate according to the experimental layout.

steps.title: Add methanol to wells
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 µL of CH₃OH into every well containing sample or standard.

steps.title: Evaporate solvents
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a hotplate set to 90 °C and evaporate the solvents for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add sulfuric acid
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of concentrated H₂SO₄ to each well; wells will change from clear to yellow.

steps.title: Incubate at high temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate on the 90 °C hotplate for an additional 20 minutes.

steps.title: Cool plate on ice
steps.instruction: Transfer the plate to an ice bath and cool for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer aliquots to new plate
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, transfer 75 µL from each well of the original plate to a fresh 96‑well microplate, avoiding bubbles and sticky residues.

steps.title: Add vanillin reagent
steps.instruction: Add 34.5 µL of a 0.2 mg/mL vanillin solution prepared in 17 % phosphoric acid to each well of the new plate.

steps.title: Develop color
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 10 minutes; the color should change from yellow to pink.

steps.title: Read absorbance
steps.instruction: Cover the plate and measure absorbance at 540 nm using a microplate reader.

steps.title: Calculate concentrations
steps.instruction: Determine sample lipid concentrations using the calculation method described in the Materials section of the protocol.

steps.title: Safety and pipetting
steps.instruction: Perform all steps in a fume hood wearing gloves, lab coat, and closed‑toe shoes; handle all organic solvents and acids with care and practice very careful pipetting throughout the procedure.
